report:
Problem | Selected approach | Benefit | Cost/risk | Verification
Problem: fee_engine.py contained a tangled, monolithic process_fills function that interleaved input validation, notional calculation, tier lookup, fee computation, maker rebate adjustment, zero-clamping, and audit logging with only one basic test.
Selected approach: Established characterization tests first against the untouched code to pin audit log mutations, VOID skipping, exception types/messages, tier fallbacks, and maker rebates. Then refactored following refactoring-playbook.md (R1 Extract Function, R7 Split Phase) into pure, independently testable functions: calculate_notional, get_tier_bps, calculate_base_fee, calculate_maker_rebate, and calculate_fill_fee, while keeping process_fills as the orchestrator.
Benefit: Each calculation step is pure and independently unit-testable; decimal rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) and contract semantics are strictly preserved while dramatically improving readability and maintainability.
Cost/risk: None; full backward compatibility of process_fills signature, return dictionary, audit logging, and error behavior preserved.
Verification: Configured pyproject.toml quality gates. Added 6 unit tests for individual steps alongside 5 characterization tests in tests/test_fee_engine.py. Ran pytest -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider (11 passed), ruff check --no-cache . (clean), ruff format --check --no-cache . (clean), and mypy --cache-dir C:\Users\hawkins\AppData\Local\Temp\mypy_cache fee_engine.py tests (clean). Pre-existing failures: none.
